In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new methodology that allows the isolation/purification of extracellular vesicle preparations from plasma, without the use of ultracentrifuges, that can be analyzed by MS and that is suitable for translational applications.
the characterization of plasma-derived vesicle proteins, in the size-range of exosomes, by a mass spectrometry-based approach.
the development of new strategies for the isolation of vesicle preparations, which are suitable for MS analysis, and the validation of novel markers of plasma-derived exosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

SEC, as a stand-alone method, is a valid alternative to ultracentrifuged exosomes, and the proteins identified in our study are good candidates for future studies on the role of plasma-derived exosomes.
SEC is a more reliable methodology to obtain vesicles from plasma and that CD5L and/or LGALS3BP are more suitable markers of vesicles than the “classical exosomal markers.”

SEC, a widely used and established methodology for the separation and purification of macromolecules, is a suitable alternative to ultracentrifuging plasma to obtain preparations of plasma-derived vesicle, in the size-range of exosomes, for mass spectrometry analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SEC, a simple, inexpensive and widely available technique, can be used to obtain vesicles, in a size range that overlaps with the size of exosomes, and that these vesicles can be characterized by MS.
SEC is the best method to isolate vesicles from plasma and CD5L and LAGALS3BP are the best exosome markers to use for plasma-derived vesicles.

the use of SEC to isolate extracellular vesicles from plasma, followed by MS, is a promising approach to characterize plasma-derived vesicles and that CD5L and galectin 3 binding protein (LGALS-3BP) are more suitable plasma-derived vesicle markers in MS than CD63 or TSG101.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the characterization of the protein content in plasma sub-components, in the size-range of exosomes, is feasible with SEC, a method that does not require ultracentrifugations, and can be used to identify markers that are suitable to be detected by MS.

the characterization of the protein content of plasma-derived vesicle preparations is highly dependent on the methodology used for isolation/purification and that the presence of classical exosome markers is not necessarily indicative of vesicle enrichment.

, when MS analyses of plasma-derived extracellular vesicles are performed, it is crucial to take into account the isolation/purification methodologies, as well as the size range, and to use appropriate markers to validate the results.
